# Build Prompt: `odk-central-operators` — Production-Grade Juju K8s Charm Group

This document is a self-contained build prompt for a dev-box agent
session. The consuming agent may not be Claude Code. It runs unattended
(equivalent to `--dangerously-skip-permissions`) on a machine with
`juju`, `charmcraft`, `git`, and a bootstrapped Kubernetes. Prefer
Canonical Kubernetes (`k8s`) wherever the choice arises; microk8s is a
fallback only. No interactive checkpoints occur after Phase 0.

References to `mastodon-operator`, `sentry-operators`,
`hedgedoc-operator`, `windmill-operators`, `zammad-operator`,
`flagsmith-operators`, `tracecat-operator` and
`dependencytrack-operators` in the `tonyandrewmeyer/` namespace on
GitHub are prior operator work used here as background context on
repository conventions only. This charm group is not derived from them.

**What is being built.** ODK Central is the server half of the ODK
ecosystem: forms authored as XLSForm spreadsheets are converted to
XForms, filled in offline on a mobile client or in a browser, and
submitted back to Central. Upstream ships it as an eight-container
Docker Compose stack. This build produces **three charms** in one
repository, deployed as a group, plus the two charm libraries that bind
them together.

Desk recon and scoring for this candidate: `RECON-odk-central.md` in
`non-roadmap/own-a-charm/` of the work-queue repo. Category context:
`RECON-forms.md`. Read neither to build — everything needed is below.

---

## USER ANSWERS REQUIRED — Read Before Phase 0

Collect all answers before running Phase 0. The build does not pause
again after Phase 0 completes.

```
Q1 — GitHub namespace
     Which GitHub user or organisation hosts the repo?
     Default: tonyandrewmeyer
     The repository will be created at <namespace>/odk-central-operators.
     It holds all three charms; there is no separate repo per charm.

Q2 — Juju k8s controller name
     What is the name of the bootstrapped Kubernetes controller?
     Run to list available: juju controllers --format=yaml
     Canonical Kubernetes (k8s) is preferred over microk8s. If both are
     bootstrapped, use the k8s one.

Q3 — ODK Central version to target
     Which release should the charms pin on day one?
     To find the latest, list the tags on the official image:
       TOKEN=$(curl -s "https://ghcr.io/token?scope=repository:getodk/central-service:pull&service=ghcr.io" | jq -r .token)
       curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
         https://ghcr.io/v2/getodk/central-service/tags/list | jq -r '.tags[-5:]'
     Recommended starting point as of 2026-08-25: v2026.2.4
     Write the tag with the leading "v": v2026.2.4
     The same tag pins BOTH central-service and central-nginx — they are
     released together and must not be mismatched.

Q4 — Enketo and pyxform versions
     Enketo default: 7.6.1  (ghcr.io/enketo/enketo)
     pyxform default: v4.5.0 (ghcr.io/getodk/pyxform-http)
     These are pinned independently of Q3. Confirm the versions the
     chosen Central release expects by reading enketo.dockerfile and
     docker-compose.yml at the Q3 tag of getodk/central:
       https://raw.githubusercontent.com/getodk/central/<Q3>/enketo.dockerfile
       https://raw.githubusercontent.com/getodk/central/<Q3>/docker-compose.yml
     If those files name different versions, the upstream files win.

Q5 — Redis backing for Enketo
     Enketo needs two Redis instances with different persistence
     semantics. Charmhub has no stable Redis charm (redis-k8s is
     latest/edge revision 23, released 2022-12-05).
     Default: in-charm — run both as sidecar containers inside
     enketo-k8s, with Juju filesystem storage for the durable one.
     Alternative: relate — wire optional redis-main / redis-cache
     relations and deploy redis-k8s from latest/edge.
     Default: in-charm (the relations are still declared and take
     precedence when present; see Architecture Decisions).
     Answer: in-charm or relate

Q6 — Public domain name
     The fully qualified domain the deployment will be reached at.
     ODK Central will not work with a bare IP address — the frontend
     bakes the origin into its client config and Enketo's linked-server
     URL must match.
     For a test deploy, a nip.io style name against the traefik
     external IP is acceptable, e.g. odk.10-0-0-5.nip.io
     Example: odk.example.com

Q7 — Initial admin email
     Email address for the first Central web user, which the
     create-admin action promotes to administrator.
     Stored as a Juju secret, never in charm config.
     Example: ops-team@example.com

Q8 — Day-one authentication mode
     Options: password, oidc
     Default: password
     IMPORTANT: these are mutually exclusive upstream. With OIDC
     enabled, HTTP Basic auth and POST /v1/session stop working
     entirely. This answer controls what Phase 4's smoke test and the
     Phase 10 integration suite authenticate with. OIDC is wired and
     tested in Phase 8 regardless of this answer.

Q9 — Charmhub entity names and track
     Defaults: odk-central-k8s, enketo-k8s, pyxform-k8s
     Default track: latest
     Central uses date-based versions (2026.2.x), so a version track
     would need renaming every quarter; latest/edge → latest/candidate
     is the intended promotion path. Confirm or supply alternatives.

Q10 — Error reporting
     Upstream's shipped compose defaults contain ODK's OWN Sentry DSN,
     organisation subdomain and project key. A naive deploy reports
     errors to the ODK project's telemetry.
     Default: disabled — the charm blanks every SENTRY_* value unless
     an operator sets its own DSN via config.
     Answer: disabled, or supply your own DSN.
```

---

## Architecture Decisions (pre-resolved)

These decisions are final. Do not re-debate them during the build.

**Kubernetes-only for v1.** `postgresql-k8s`, `traefik-k8s`,
`s3-integrator`, `smtp-integrator` and the COS charms all have mature
k8s variants, and upstream ships only container images. A machine charm
is out of scope for this build.

**Three Juju applications, seven containers.** The group is:

| Charm | Containers | Why separate |
|---|---|---|
| `odk-central-k8s` | `service`, `nginx` | The API and the frontend/reverse-proxy are released together and version-locked; they belong in one application |
| `enketo-k8s` | `enketo`, plus `redis-main` and `redis-cache` under Q5 default | Enketo is an independently versioned upstream (`enketo/enketo`) with its own state; it scales and upgrades on its own cadence |
| `pyxform-k8s` | `pyxform` | A stateless XLSForm→XForm converter with its own release train; separating it makes the conversion service replaceable and independently scalable |

Do not collapse these into one application. The cross-charm bootstrap
ordering and the provided interface are the point of the exercise.

**`SSL_TYPE=upstream`.** Upstream's nginx image can obtain Let's
Encrypt certificates itself. In Juju, TLS is `traefik-k8s`'s job. Set
`SSL_TYPE=upstream` so nginx serves plain HTTP on 80 and trusts
`X-Forwarded-Proto`. Never enable certbot inside the charm.

**No `secrets` container.** Upstream's one-shot `secrets` container
writes three files to a shared Docker volume. Juju has no shared volume
between applications, so `odk-central-k8s` generates all three values
in its `install` hook, stores them as application-owned Juju secrets,
and distributes them to `enketo-k8s` over the `odk-enketo` relation.
This is the charm-group design's centrepiece.

**Exact secret lengths are load-bearing.**
`files/enketo/start-enketo.sh` upstream asserts, with `stat -c "%s"`,
that `/etc/secrets/enketo-secret` is exactly **64** bytes,
`/etc/secrets/enketo-less-secret` exactly **32** bytes, and
`/etc/secrets/enketo-api-key` exactly **128** bytes. Enketo refuses to
start otherwise. When the `enketo-k8s` charm pushes these files with
Pebble, write **no trailing newline** and assert the length in charm
code before pushing. A stray `\n` is a 65-byte file and a hard startup
failure with an unhelpful message.

**Two new charm libraries, written here.** No published charmlib exists
for either interface. Write and ship:

- `lib/charms/odk_central_k8s/v0/odk_enketo.py` — `OdkEnketoProvider`
  (in `odk-central-k8s`) and `OdkEnketoRequirer` (in `enketo-k8s`).
  Provider sends: secret IDs for the three shared secrets, and the
  public base URL. Requirer sends back: the in-cluster Enketo URL that
  Central puts in `config.json` under `enketo.url`.
- `lib/charms/pyxform_k8s/v0/xlsform.py` — `XlsformProvider` (in
  `pyxform-k8s`) and `XlsformRequirer` (in `odk-central-k8s`).
  Provider sends host and port; requirer consumes them into
  `config.json` under `xlsform`.

Both are bidirectional; model them on `data_platform_libs` conventions
for event naming (`*_ready`, `*_gone`) and emit custom events rather
than making the charm handle raw `relation-changed`.

**Charm libraries over hand-rolled requirers everywhere else.** Where a
published charmlib exists for a relation interface, import it. Hand
rolling is acceptable only for the two ODK-specific interfaces above.

**Redis default is in-charm (Q5).** `redis-main` and `redis-cache` run
as sidecar containers in `enketo-k8s`, `redis-main` mounting a Juju
`filesystem` storage at `/data` with upstream's persistence settings
(`save 300 1`, `appendonly no`, `dbfilename enketo-main.rdb`) and
`redis-cache` running with persistence off. The charm ALSO declares
optional `redis-main` and `redis-cache` relations (interface `redis`);
when either is related, the corresponding sidecar is stopped and the
relation endpoint is used instead. Attempt the relation path once in
Phase 6 against `redis-k8s --channel latest/edge` and record the result
in `docs/day2-ops.md` whichever way it goes.

**`jubilant` for integration tests, `ops.testing` for unit tests.** Do
not use `pytest-operator`.

**Juju secrets for every credential.** No password, key, token or DSN
appears in `config:`.

**`charmcraft 4.x` + `ops 3.x`.** Verify at Phase 0; if newer minors
are available, use them. Do not pin below these majors.

**Apache 2.0 for the charms.** The upstream workload is Apache-2.0
throughout — `getodk/central`, `central-backend`, `central-frontend`
and `enketo/enketo` — so unlike most candidates in this category there
is no licence divergence to document. Say so explicitly in
`CONTRIBUTING.md`; it is the reason this upstream was chosen.

**`mkdocs-material` for the docs site**, one site for all three charms.

**`release-please` for release automation**, `uv` for Python
dependency management, Conventional Commits throughout.

**Commit directly to `origin/main`.** No feature branches. Each phase
ends with a commit and `git push -u origin main`.

---

## ODK Central Component Map

Sourced from `docker-compose.yml`, `.env.template`,
`files/service/config.json.template`,
`files/enketo/config.json.template`,
`files/enketo/start-enketo.sh` and
`files/enketo/redis-enketo-main.conf` at `getodk/central` master,
verified 2026-08-25. Re-verify at the Q3 tag before writing code.

### Services and their roles

| Upstream service | Image | Charm | Pebble service | Mandatory? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `service` | `ghcr.io/getodk/central-service:<Q3>` | odk-central-k8s | `service` | Yes |
| `nginx` | `ghcr.io/getodk/central-nginx:<Q3>` | odk-central-k8s | `nginx` | Yes |
| `enketo` | `ghcr.io/enketo/enketo:<Q4>` | enketo-k8s | `enketo` | Yes |
| `enketo_redis_main` | `redis:8.6.4` | enketo-k8s | `redis-main` | Yes (or relation) |
| `enketo_redis_cache` | `redis:8.6.4` | enketo-k8s | `redis-cache` | Yes (or relation) |
| `pyxform` | `ghcr.io/getodk/pyxform-http:<Q4>` | pyxform-k8s | `pyxform` | Yes |
| `secrets` | — | none | — | Replaced by charm-generated Juju secrets |
| `postgres14` | — | none | — | `postgresql-k8s` relation |
| `mail` | — | none | — | `smtp-integrator` relation |

`postgres` (the 9.6→14 upgrade helper) has no charm equivalent and is
not built. Note it in `docs/day2-ops.md` under migration-from-compose.

### Pebble service startup order

**`odk-central-k8s`:**

1. Block until `postgresql` relation data is complete.
2. Render `/usr/odk/config/local.json` (or wherever the image expects
   its config — verify against the image, see Phase 4) from the
   template, including database, email, xlsform, enketo, oidc and
   s3blobStore stanzas.
3. Run migrations as a one-shot Pebble service (`migrations`,
   `startup: disabled`, started by charm code, exit code checked).
4. Start `service`; gate `ActiveStatus` on
   `GET http://localhost:8383/v1/version.json` returning 200.
5. Start `nginx` only once `service` is healthy — the nginx config
   proxies to it and will fail its own healthcheck otherwise.

`nginx` additionally needs `DOMAIN`, `SSL_TYPE=upstream`, `HTTPS_PORT`
and `OIDC_ENABLED` in its environment because it templates
`client-config.json` for the browser at container start. Changing any
of those is a **re-render and reload**, not just a restart: the file is
read by the frontend at page load.

**`enketo-k8s`:**

1. Start `redis-main` and `redis-cache` (or verify the relations).
2. Block until the `odk-enketo` relation supplies all three secrets and
   the base URL.
3. Push `/etc/secrets/enketo-secret` (64 B), `enketo-less-secret`
   (32 B), `enketo-api-key` (128 B) with exact lengths, no newline.
4. Render `config.json` from the template with `SECRET`,
   `LESS_SECRET`, `API_KEY`, `BASE_URL`, `DOMAIN` and the two Redis
   endpoints.
5. Start `enketo`; gate `ActiveStatus` on port 8005 accepting
   connections.

**`pyxform-k8s`:** single service, starts immediately, no dependencies.
It is the only charm in the group that can reach `ActiveStatus`
standalone.

### Cross-charm bootstrap ordering

```
pyxform-k8s ──(xlsform)──▶ odk-central-k8s ──(odk-enketo)──▶ enketo-k8s
                                  ▲                                │
                                  └──── enketo URL sent back ──────┘
```

`odk-central-k8s` cannot render a complete `config.json` until BOTH the
`xlsform` relation (host/port) and the `odk-enketo` relation (Enketo's
URL, which Enketo only sends after it has received the secrets Central
generated) are settled. That is a genuine two-way bootstrap: Central
must publish secrets before Enketo can start, and Enketo must publish
its URL before Central's config is complete.

Implement it as: Central writes secrets and base URL immediately on
relation-created; Central starts with `enketo.url` pointing at a
placeholder and sets `WaitingStatus("waiting for enketo")`; on
receiving Enketo's URL it re-renders and restarts `service`. Do **not**
block Central's startup on Enketo — that deadlocks the group.

### External ports (charm-internal; traefik maps these)

- `service`: 8383 (HTTP, API)
- `nginx`: 80 (HTTP, serves frontend + proxies `/v1` to service and
  `/-` to Enketo)
- `enketo`: 8005 (HTTP)
- `pyxform`: 80 (HTTP)
- `redis-main`: 6379, `redis-cache`: 6380 (note the non-default port on
  the cache instance — upstream's config sets it and Enketo's config
  expects it)

### Storage requirements

- `odk-central-k8s`: none. All state is in PostgreSQL and, once the S3
  relation exists, the blob store.
- `enketo-k8s`: `redis-main-data`, `type: filesystem`,
  `minimum-size: 1G`, mounted at `/data` in the `redis-main`
  container. `redis-cache` is deliberately ephemeral.
- `pyxform-k8s`: none.

Losing `redis-main` loses in-flight form and instance state in Enketo.
Say so in `docs/day2-ops.md` — it is the one piece of state in the
group that is not in PostgreSQL or S3.

---

## Relation Surface

Fetch the published libraries below after `charmcraft init` and before
writing any relation-handling code. If a `charmcraft fetch-lib` command
returns 404, inspect the charm's Charmhub "Libraries" tab at
`https://charmhub.io/<charm-name>` and update this list.

```bash
# PostgreSQL — Central's application database
charmcraft fetch-lib charms.data_platform_libs.v0.data_interfaces

# Traefik — HTTP ingress
charmcraft fetch-lib charms.traefik_k8s.v2.ingress

# S3 — blob store for submission attachments and form media
charmcraft fetch-lib charms.data_platform_libs.v0.s3

# SMTP — account creation and password reset email
charmcraft fetch-lib charms.smtp_integrator.v0.smtp

# OIDC — Canonical Identity Platform (hydra) provides the oauth interface
charmcraft fetch-lib charms.hydra.v0.oauth

# TLS certificates (for a self-signed test model)
charmcraft fetch-lib charms.tls_certificates_interface.v4.tls_certificates

# COS-Lite observability
charmcraft fetch-lib charms.loki_k8s.v1.loki_push_api
charmcraft fetch-lib charms.prometheus_k8s.v0.prometheus_scrape
charmcraft fetch-lib charms.grafana_k8s.v0.grafana_dashboard
charmcraft fetch-lib charms.tempo_coordinator_k8s.v0.tracing
```

### Relation matrix

**`odk-central-k8s`:**

```yaml
provides:
  odk-enketo:
    interface: odk-enketo
    limit: 1
requires:
  postgresql:
    interface: postgresql_client
    limit: 1
  xlsform:
    interface: odk-xlsform
    limit: 1
  ingress:
    interface: ingress
    limit: 1
  s3:
    interface: s3
    limit: 1
  smtp:
    interface: smtp
    limit: 1
  oauth:
    interface: oauth
    limit: 1
  logging:
    interface: loki_push_api
  metrics-endpoint:
    interface: prometheus_scrape
  grafana-dashboard:
    interface: grafana_dashboard
  tracing:
    interface: tracing
    limit: 1
```

**`enketo-k8s`:**

```yaml
requires:
  odk-enketo:
    interface: odk-enketo
    limit: 1
  redis-main:
    interface: redis
    limit: 1
    optional: true
  redis-cache:
    interface: redis
    limit: 1
    optional: true
  logging:
    interface: loki_push_api
  metrics-endpoint:
    interface: prometheus_scrape
  grafana-dashboard:
    interface: grafana_dashboard
```

**`pyxform-k8s`:**

```yaml
provides:
  xlsform:
    interface: odk-xlsform
requires:
  logging:
    interface: loki_push_api
  metrics-endpoint:
    interface: prometheus_scrape
```

`pyxform` has no ingress: it is reached only by Central, in-cluster.
Do not expose it.

### Composition model for integration tests

```bash
juju deploy ./odk-central-k8s_amd64.charm odk-central-k8s \
  --resource service-image=ghcr.io/getodk/central-service:<Q3> \
  --resource nginx-image=ghcr.io/getodk/central-nginx:<Q3> --trust
juju deploy ./enketo-k8s_amd64.charm enketo-k8s \
  --resource enketo-image=ghcr.io/enketo/enketo:<Q4> \
  --resource redis-image=redis:8.6.4
juju deploy ./pyxform-k8s_amd64.charm pyxform-k8s \
  --resource pyxform-image=ghcr.io/getodk/pyxform-http:<Q4>

juju deploy postgresql-k8s --channel 16/stable --trust
juju deploy traefik-k8s --channel latest/stable --trust
juju deploy s3-integrator --channel latest/stable
juju deploy smtp-integrator --channel latest/stable

juju integrate odk-central-k8s postgresql-k8s
juju integrate odk-central-k8s pyxform-k8s
juju integrate odk-central-k8s enketo-k8s
juju integrate odk-central-k8s traefik-k8s
juju integrate odk-central-k8s s3-integrator
juju integrate odk-central-k8s smtp-integrator

# COS-Lite (optional in Phases 1-9, required in Phase 9)
juju integrate odk-central-k8s loki-k8s
juju integrate odk-central-k8s prometheus-k8s
juju integrate odk-central-k8s grafana-k8s
juju integrate odk-central-k8s tempo-coordinator-k8s
juju integrate enketo-k8s loki-k8s
juju integrate pyxform-k8s loki-k8s
```

## Configuration & Secret Surface

### `odk-central-k8s` config

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `external-hostname` | string | `""` | Public FQDN (Q6). Overrides the ingress-supplied hostname when set. Central will not work with a bare IP |
| `sysadmin-email` | string | `""` | Address shown to users as the system contact; also used as the Let's Encrypt contact upstream, unused here |
| `email-from` | string | `""` | Envelope From for outbound mail. Defaults to `no-reply@<external-hostname>` when empty |
| `session-lifetime` | int | `86400` | Web session lifetime in seconds |
| `db-pool-size` | int | `10` | Per-worker PostgreSQL connection pool size |
| `log-level` | string | `INFO` | Workload log level: `DEBUG`, `INFO`, `WARN`, `ERROR` |
| `oidc-enabled` | bool | `false` | Enable OpenID Connect. **Disables password auth and `POST /v1/session` entirely** — see Phase 8 |
| `oidc-issuer-url` | string | `""` | OIDC issuer URL. Ignored when the `oauth` relation is present, which supplies it |
| `oidc-client-id` | string | `""` | OIDC client ID (public, non-sensitive). Ignored when the `oauth` relation is present |
| `s3-bucket-name` | string | `""` | Override the bucket name supplied by the `s3` relation |
| `s3-upload-interval-minutes` | int | `15` | How often the charm triggers the pending-blob upload job |
| `error-reporting-dsn` | string | `""` | Operator's own Sentry DSN. Empty means all `SENTRY_*` values are blanked — upstream's shipped defaults are ODK's own project and must never be inherited (Q10) |
| `frontend-analytics-enabled` | bool | `false` | Whether Central offers the upstream usage-reporting prompt to administrators |

### `enketo-k8s` config

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `offline-enabled` | bool | `true` | Allow offline-capable web forms (service worker) |
| `payload-limit` | string | `1mb` | Maximum submission payload accepted by Enketo |
| `text-field-character-limit` | int | `1000000` | Upstream default; lower it for constrained deployments |
| `exclude-non-relevant` | bool | `true` | Do not submit values for questions hidden by relevance logic |
| `redis-main-maxmemory` | string | `""` | Optional `maxmemory` for the in-charm durable instance |
| `redis-cache-maxmemory` | string | `256mb` | `maxmemory` for the in-charm cache instance |
| `log-level` | string | `INFO` | Workload log level |

### `pyxform-k8s` config

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `workers` | int | `2` | HTTP worker processes |
| `conversion-timeout` | int | `60` | Seconds before an XLSForm conversion is abandoned |
| `log-level` | string | `INFO` | Workload log level |

### Secret surface (Juju secrets — never `config:`)

Secrets with no operator-supplied value are generated by
`odk-central-k8s` on first `install`. Operator-supplied ones are marked
**OPERATOR-PROVIDED**.

| Juju secret label | Contents | Source | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `odk-enketo-api-key` | Exactly **128** characters | Generated | Shared with Enketo over the relation; also written into Central's own `enketo.apiKey` |
| `odk-enketo-secret` | Exactly **64** characters | Generated | Enketo's encryption key |
| `odk-enketo-less-secret` | Exactly **32** characters | Generated | Enketo's "less secure" encryption key |
| `odk-admin-email` | Email string | **OPERATOR-PROVIDED** (Q7) | Consumed by the `create-admin` action |
| `odk-admin-password` | Password string | Generated if absent | Returned once by `create-admin`; never logged |
| `odk-oidc-client-secret` | OIDC client secret | **OPERATOR-PROVIDED** | Only when `oidc-enabled=true` and no `oauth` relation |
| — | S3 access/secret key | `s3` relation | Never a Juju secret owned by this charm |
| — | SMTP user/password | `smtp` relation | Never a Juju secret owned by this charm |

Generate with `secrets.token_urlsafe()` trimmed (or
`secrets.choice` over an explicit alphabet) to the **exact** lengths
above, then assert `len(value) == N` before storing. Store via
`self.app.add_secret({...}, label=...)`; on later hooks retrieve rather
than regenerate.

```bash
SECRET_ID=$(juju secret add odk-admin-email email=<Q7-value> --format json | jq -r .secret-id)
juju grant-secret $SECRET_ID odk-central-k8s
juju config odk-central-k8s admin-email-secret=$SECRET_ID
```

### Relation and config → `config.json` mapping

Central reads a JSON config file, not environment variables. The charm
renders it; upstream's `files/service/config.json.template` is the
authoritative shape.

| `config.json` path | Source |
|---|---|
| `database.host` / `.user` / `.password` / `.database` | `postgresql` relation |
| `database.maximumPoolSize` | `db-pool-size` config |
| `email.serviceAccount` | `email-from` config |
| `email.transportOpts.host` / `.port` / `.secure` / `.auth.*` | `smtp` relation |
| `sessionLifetime` | `session-lifetime` config |

| Env var | Source |
|---|---|
| `DOMAIN` | ingress URL host or `external-hostname` |
| `SSL_TYPE` | hardcoded `upstream` |
| `HTTPS_PORT` | hardcoded `443` |

| `config.json` path | Source |
|---|---|

## Phase 0 — Pre-flight & Answers

**Goals:** Verify the dev box is ready; print a build manifest; block
on any missing prerequisite before writing a line of charm code.

**Steps:**

1. Verify tool versions:
   ```bash
   juju version          # must be >= 3.6
   charmcraft version    # must be >= 4.0
   git --version
   python3 --version     # must be >= 3.12
   uv --version          # install: curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh
   ```

2. Verify the k8s controller (Q2) and prefer Canonical Kubernetes:
   ```bash
   juju controllers --format=yaml
   juju switch <Q2-controller>
   juju status --format=yaml | head -5
   ```

3. Verify the GitHub repository exists or can be created at
   `<Q1>/odk-central-operators`. If it does not exist, create it empty.

4. Confirm every image tag resolves before pinning it:
   ```bash
   for img in "getodk/central-service:<Q3>" "getodk/central-nginx:<Q3>" \
              "getodk/pyxform-http:<Q4-pyxform>" "enketo/enketo:<Q4-enketo>"; do
     repo="${img%:*}"; tag="${img##*:}"
     tok=$(curl -s "https://ghcr.io/token?scope=repository:$repo:pull&service=ghcr.io" | jq -r .token)
     code=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $tok" \
       "https://ghcr.io/v2/$repo/manifests/$tag" \
       -H "Accept: application/vnd.oci.image.index.v1+json")
     echo "$img -> $code"   # 200 required
   done
   ```

5. Download the upstream reference files for the Q3 tag into `hack/upstream/`
   and keep them in the repo as the source of truth for later phases:
   ```bash
   mkdir -p hack/upstream
   base=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/getodk/central/<Q3>
   for f in docker-compose.yml .env.template enketo.dockerfile \
            files/service/config.json.template \
            files/enketo/config.json.template \
            files/enketo/start-enketo.sh \
            files/enketo/redis-enketo-main.conf \
            files/enketo/redis-enketo-cache.conf \
            files/nginx/odk.conf.template \
            files/nginx/client-config.json.template; do
     curl -sfSL "$base/$f" -o "hack/upstream/$(basename $f)" || echo "MISSING: $f"
   done
   ```
   If any file is missing at that tag, the upstream layout has changed
   — re-derive the component map from what is actually there before
   continuing. Upstream files always win over this document.

6. Print a one-page build manifest summarising Q1–Q10 and the installed
   tool versions. Proceed immediately if unattended.

**Commit:** none — Phase 0 is pre-work only.

   actions:
     create-admin:
       description: |
         Create the initial web user from the odk-admin-email Juju
         secret and promote it to administrator. Returns the generated

other two follow.

## Phase 4 — `odk-central-k8s` Single-Container Baseline

**Goals:** The Central API service runs under Pebble against a
PostgreSQL relation; migrations run before the service starts; the
charm reports `active/idle`; `/v1/version.json` answers.

Phase 4 deliberately excludes nginx, Enketo, S3, SMTP and OIDC. Render
`config.json` with the `xlsform` stanza from the Phase 3 relation, an
`enketo.url` placeholder, empty `s3blobStore`, blanked `sentry`, and a
null email transport. Central starts without a working mail transport;
it only fails when something tries to send.

**Steps:**

1. Determine where the image expects its config and how it starts:
   ```bash
   docker create --name tmp-svc ghcr.io/getodk/central-service:<Q3>
   docker inspect tmp-svc --format='{{json .Config.Entrypoint}} {{json .Config.Cmd}} {{json .Config.WorkingDir}}'
   docker export tmp-svc | tar -t | grep -E 'start-odk|config/(local|default)\.json' | head
   docker rm tmp-svc
   ```
   `hack/upstream/config.json.template` gives the required shape;
   the image's own `start-odk.sh` gives the path and the render step.
   **The image's files are authoritative** — this document is not.

2. Implement `_render_service_config()` returning the full
   `config.json` dict from the mapping table above, and push it with
   `container.push(path, json.dumps(cfg, indent=2), make_dirs=True)`.

3. Pebble layer for the `service` container:
   ```python
   ops.pebble.Layer({
       "summary": "odk central service",
       "services": {
           "migrations": {
               "override": "replace",
               "summary": "database migrations (one-shot)",
               "command": "<verified migration command>",
               "startup": "disabled",
               "environment": self._service_env(),
           },
           "service": {
               "override": "replace",
               "summary": "ODK Central API",
               "command": "<verified start command>",
               "startup": "disabled",
               "environment": self._service_env(),
               "on-failure": "restart",
           },
       },
       "checks": {
           "api-up": {
               "override": "replace",
               "level": "ready",
               "period": "15s",
               "threshold": 3,
               "http": {"url": "http://localhost:8383/v1/version.json"},
           },
       },
   })
   ```

4. Startup sequence, driven from a single `_reconcile()` that every
   hook calls (do not scatter logic across per-relation handlers):
   1. Return early with `WaitingStatus` if the `postgresql` relation is
      incomplete.
   2. Generate the three Enketo secrets if absent (they are needed here
      even before `enketo-k8s` exists, because `enketo.apiKey` is part
      of Central's own config).
   3. Render and push `config.json`.
   4. `container.start("migrations")`; poll until the service exits;
      non-zero exit → `BlockedStatus("database migration failed")` and
      return.
   5. Start `service`; wait for the `api-up` check to pass.
   6. `ActiveStatus("api ready; awaiting enketo")` until the
      `odk-enketo` relation is settled.

5. Unit tests: postgres relation complete → migrations run then service
   starts; postgres incomplete → Waiting; migration non-zero exit →
   Blocked; secrets generated once and reused on re-run; secret lengths
   are exactly 128/64/32.

6. Smoke test:
   ```bash
   juju deploy ./charms/odk-central-k8s/odk-central-k8s_amd64.charm \
     --resource service-image=ghcr.io/getodk/central-service:<Q3> \
     --resource nginx-image=ghcr.io/getodk/central-nginx:<Q3> --trust
   juju deploy postgresql-k8s --channel 16/stable --trust
   juju integrate odk-central-k8s postgresql-k8s
   juju integrate odk-central-k8s pyxform-k8s
   juju wait-for application odk-central-k8s --query='status=="active"' --timeout=15m
   juju ssh --container service odk-central-k8s/0 \
     curl -s http://localhost:8383/v1/version.json
   ```

7. Commit: `feat(central): postgresql relation, config render, migrations, api service`.

**Definition of done:** `active/idle`; `/v1/version.json` returns the
Q3 version; unit tests green.

**Goals:** The `nginx` container serves the built frontend and proxies
the API; `traefik-k8s` fronts it; the web UI loads in a browser.

1. Wire `IngressPerAppRequirer` from
   `charms.traefik_k8s.v2.ingress`, requesting port 80 (nginx), not

   `hack/upstream/client-config.json.template` to confirm which
   variables the image's entrypoint substitutes; supply every one of
   them, including the ones you are blanking.

3. **Config changes to `DOMAIN`, `OIDC_ENABLED` or the Sentry values
   are a re-render and reload, not a restart.** The browser reads
   `client-config.json` on page load. Implement
   `_reload_nginx()` as a Pebble `exec` of `nginx -s reload` after the
   entrypoint's templating step has been re-run, and unit-test that a

## Phase 6 — `enketo-k8s`, Shared Secrets and the Provided Interface

**Goals:** The group's centrepiece. `odk-central-k8s` provides three
generated secrets over the `odk-enketo` relation; `enketo-k8s` consumes
them, runs its two Redis instances, and publishes its URL back;
Central re-renders and restarts with a real `enketo.url`.

**Steps:**

1. Complete `lib/charms/odk_central_k8s/v0/odk_enketo.py`.

   Provider (`odk-central-k8s`), on relation-created and on any change
   to the secrets or the base URL:
   ```python
   self.model.get_secret(label="odk-enketo-api-key").grant(relation)
   self.model.get_secret(label="odk-enketo-secret").grant(relation)
   self.model.get_secret(label="odk-enketo-less-secret").grant(relation)
   relation.data[self.app].update({
       "api-key-secret-id": ...,
       "encryption-key-secret-id": ...,
       "less-secure-key-secret-id": ...,
       "base-url": self._public_base_url(),
       "support-email": self.config["sysadmin-email"],
   })
   ```
   Requirer (`enketo-k8s`) reads the IDs, calls
   `self.model.get_secret(id=...)`, and emits `OdkEnketoReadyEvent`.
   Requirer writes back `enketo-url` (`http://<bind-address>:8005/-`);
   the provider emits `EnketoUrlChangedEvent`.

2. Write the three secret files into the `enketo` container **before**
   starting it:
   ```python
   for path, label, length in (
       ("/etc/secrets/enketo-secret", "odk-enketo-secret", 64),
       ("/etc/secrets/enketo-less-secret", "odk-enketo-less-secret", 32),
       ("/etc/secrets/enketo-api-key", "odk-enketo-api-key", 128),
   ):
       value = secret_content[label]
       if len(value.encode()) != length:      # not len(value) — bytes
           raise RuntimeError(f"{label} must be exactly {length} bytes")
       container.push(path, value, make_dirs=True, permissions=0o400)
   ```
   No trailing newline. `start-enketo.sh` stats the files and aborts on
   any other size.

3. Render Enketo's `config.json` from
   `hack/upstream/config.json.template` (the Enketo one) using the
   mapping table above, and push it to the path
   `start-enketo.sh` expects. Set `hide powered by` and the logo
   fields as upstream does.

4. Redis containers (Q5 default `in-charm`): two Pebble services in
   two containers using the same `redis-image` resource, each with its
   own config file pushed by the charm from
   `hack/upstream/redis-enketo-main.conf` and
   `redis-enketo-cache.conf`, with `maxmemory` overridden from charm
   config. `redis-main` mounts the `redis-main-data` storage at
   `/data`. **Keep the cache on port 6380** — Enketo's config expects
   it and changing it silently breaks nothing until cache lookups start
   failing.

5. Optional relation override: if a `redis-main` or `redis-cache`
   relation is present, stop the corresponding sidecar, point Enketo's
   config at the relation endpoint, and set a status message naming
   which instances are relation-backed.

6. **Attempt the relation path once**, whatever Q5 said:
   ```bash
   juju deploy redis-k8s --channel latest/edge
   juju integrate enketo-k8s:redis-cache redis-k8s
   ```
   Record what happens — deploys and works, deploys and misbehaves, or
   fails outright — in `docs/day2-ops.md` under "Redis backing". This
   is a genuinely open question (Charmhub has no stable Redis charm;
   `redis-k8s` is `latest/edge` revision 23 from 2022-12-05) and the
   answer is useful independently of this charm. Then remove the
   relation and continue with the Q5 choice.

7. Central side: on `EnketoUrlChangedEvent`, re-render `config.json`
   with the real `enketo.url` and restart `service`. Do not restart
   nginx.

8. Unit tests, both charms:
   - secrets granted and IDs published on relation-created;
   - a 65-byte secret raises before any Pebble push happens;
   - Enketo blocked while the relation is incomplete;
   - Central re-renders and restarts on `enketo-url` arriving;
   - relation override stops the sidecar and rewrites the config;
   - `rotate-enketo-secrets` propagates to Enketo (Phase 7 implements
     the action; assert the library path here).

9. End-to-end check — this is the first point the group actually works:
   ```bash
   juju deploy ./charms/enketo-k8s/enketo-k8s_amd64.charm \
     --resource enketo-image=ghcr.io/enketo/enketo:<Q4> \
     --resource redis-image=redis:8.6.4
   juju integrate odk-central-k8s enketo-k8s
   juju wait-for model odk-test --query='forEach(applications, app => app.status=="active")' --timeout=20m
   ```

10. Commit: `feat(enketo): shared-secret provider/requirer, redis pair, enketo workload`.

**Definition of done:** all three charms `active/idle`; Central's
rendered `config.json` contains Enketo's real in-cluster URL; Enketo
started without a secrets-size abort.

## Phase 7 — Day-2 Actions

**Goals:** Every action implemented, tested and documented, including
the cross-charm one.

**`create-admin`** — read `odk-admin-email` from the Juju secret;
generate a password if `odk-admin-password` is absent; run Central's
admin CLI in the `service` container via Pebble `exec` (upstream's
`odk-cmd` — verify the exact invocation with
`juju ssh --container service odk-central-k8s/0 odk-cmd --help`);
create the user, then promote it to administrator. Return the password
in `event.set_results()` **once**, and never log it. If OIDC is
enabled, fail with a clear message: the password is meaningless.

**`promote-user`** / **`reset-password`** — same CLI path, one user
argument each. `reset-password` must fail cleanly under OIDC.

**`rotate-enketo-secrets`** — the interesting one:
1. Set `MaintenanceStatus("rotating enketo secrets")`.
2. Generate three new values at the exact lengths.
3. Update all three Juju secrets (`secret.set_content`).
4. Republish the IDs over the `odk-enketo` relation — Enketo's
   requirer sees `secret-changed`, rewrites the three files and
   restarts its workload.
5. Re-render Central's `config.json` (the API key appears there too)
   and restart `service`.
6. Return a warning: all in-progress web form sessions are invalidated
   and users mid-submission will have to start again.
Test that step 4 actually reaches the other charm — a rotation that
updates Central and leaves Enketo on the old key produces a
403-on-every-form failure that is very hard to read from the outside.

**`run-migrations`** — start the one-shot `migrations` service, wait,
report the exit code and the last 50 log lines.

**`upload-pending-blobs`** — no-op with a clear message when there is
no `s3` relation; otherwise invoke the upstream pending-upload
entrypoint via Pebble exec and report how many blobs moved. Also wire
this on a timer: a Pebble
[`check`](https://documentation.ubuntu.com/pebble/) is the wrong tool —
use an `ops` `update-status`-driven trigger honouring
`s3-upload-interval-minutes`, or a Pebble service with a sleep loop if
the upstream tooling supports a daemon mode. Say which you chose in
`docs/day2-ops.md`.

**`purge-deleted`** — invoke Central's purge path; require
`force=true` to bypass the retention window and say so in the
description.

**`backup`** — verify the `s3` relation; `pg_dump --format=custom` via
Pebble exec against the relation's connection string; upload to
`<destination>/<timestamp>/central.dump`; also record in the results
that blobs in S3 are **not** included and that the bucket needs its own
versioning or lifecycle policy. Return the path.

**`restore`** — Maintenance status; stop `service` and `nginx`;
download; `pg_restore`; run migrations; restart; wait for `api-up`;
Active. Refuse to run if the target database is non-empty unless a
`force` param is passed.

**`enketo-k8s` actions** — `flush-cache` (FLUSHALL against the cache
instance only; refuse if pointed at the durable one) and `redis-info`
(return `INFO` from both).

**`pyxform-k8s` action** — `convert`, taking a base64 XLSForm and
returning the XForm, for diagnosis.

**Unit tests:** one per action covering happy path, missing relation,
and Pebble exec failure propagated as a failed action rather than a
charm error.

**Commit:** `feat(charms): day-2 actions across the group`.

**Definition of done:** every action runs against the deployed group;
`create-admin` yields a login that works in the UI;
`rotate-enketo-secrets` leaves both workloads consistent.

## Phase 8 — S3, SMTP and OIDC

**Goals:** The three external integrations that turn a working deploy
into a production-shaped one.

### S3 blob storage

Wire the data-platform S3 library. On relation established, populate
`external.s3blobStore` and re-render. **New blobs go to S3; existing
blobs stay in PostgreSQL until `upload-pending-blobs` moves them**, so
model that partially-migrated state explicitly in the charm's status
message (`ActiveStatus("N blobs pending upload")` when the count is
non-zero and the relation exists).

For testing, deploy MinIO as a plain k8s Deployment
(`hack/minio-test-deploy.yaml`, written in this phase) and point
`s3-integrator` at it:
```bash
juju deploy s3-integrator --channel latest/stable
juju config s3-integrator endpoint=http://minio.default.svc:9000 \
  bucket=odk-central region=us-east-1 path=/
juju run s3-integrator/0 sync-s3-credentials access-key=... secret-key=...
juju integrate odk-central-k8s s3-integrator
```

### SMTP

Wire `charms.smtp_integrator.v0.smtp`. Populate
`email.transportOpts`. Central sends on account creation, password
reset and project invitation only, so verify with a real action rather
than a passive check:
```bash
juju deploy smtp-integrator --channel latest/stable
juju config smtp-integrator host=... port=587 auth_type=plain
juju integrate odk-central-k8s smtp-integrator
juju run odk-central-k8s/0 reset-password email=<Q7>
```
With no SMTP relation, Central must still reach Active — email failure
is a per-operation error upstream, not a startup one. Set a status
message noting that account email is unavailable.

### OIDC

Two paths, both supported:

- **Related:** `charms.hydra.v0.oauth` — request the authorisation code
  flow with scopes `openid profile email` and the redirect URI
  `https://<domain>/v1/oidc/callback` (verify the exact path against
  the Q3 release's backend source). Populate `oidc.*` from the
  relation.
- **Configured:** `oidc-enabled`, `oidc-issuer-url`, `oidc-client-id`
  config plus the `odk-oidc-client-secret` Juju secret, for a provider
  with no charm.

Relation data wins over config when both are present; say so in the
status message rather than silently preferring one.

**The mode switch is the part to get right.** Enabling OIDC disables
HTTP Basic and `POST /v1/session` upstream. So:
- `oidc-enabled=true` must also set `OIDC_ENABLED=true` in the nginx
  environment and re-render `client-config.json`, or the frontend
  offers a password form that cannot work.
- The charm's own health check must stay on the unauthenticated
  `/v1/version.json`, never on a session-creating endpoint.
- `create-admin`, `promote-user` and `reset-password` must fail with a
  clear message under OIDC, not with a CLI stack trace.
- Toggling `oidc-enabled` on a running deploy locks out every existing
  password user. Emit a warning in the status message and document it
  in `docs/day2-ops.md` as a one-way door in practice.

Unit tests: relation-over-config precedence; nginx re-render on toggle;
password actions blocked under OIDC; health check unaffected.

**Commit:** `feat(central): s3 blob store, smtp, oidc via hydra or config`.

**Definition of done:** a submission attachment lands in the MinIO
bucket; `reset-password` delivers mail; with `oidc-enabled=true` the
UI redirects to the provider and a login round-trips.

## Phase 9 — Observability

**Goals:** COS-Lite first class across all three charms.

**Loki.** `LogProxyConsumer` in each charm, forwarding every Pebble
service's logs: `service`, `nginx`, `enketo`, `redis-main`,
`redis-cache`, `pyxform`. Verify the actual on-disk log paths inside
each container rather than assuming
`/var/log/pebble/<service>/<service>.log`.

**Prometheus.** Check first whether Central exposes metrics:
```bash
juju ssh --container service odk-central-k8s/0 curl -s http://localhost:8383/metrics | head
```
If it does, use `MetricsEndpointProvider` with a static target on 8383.
If it does not, ship an `exporter` Pebble service in the `service`
container: a small `prometheus_client` process that authenticates with
a dedicated Central app-user token and exposes gauges for project
count, form count, submissions in the last hour, and pending-blob
count. Do **not** poll the API more often than every 60 seconds. Redis
metrics: run `redis_exporter` alongside each instance, or parse `INFO`
in the same exporter — either is acceptable, pick one and say which.

**Tempo.** Wire the `tracing` charmlib and set
`OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT` in the `service` environment. Check
whether `central-backend` instruments with OpenTelemetry (search the
upstream source for `opentelemetry`); if it does not, do not fake it —
wire the relation, note in `docs/observability.md` that the workload
emits no spans today, and leave it there. A tracing relation that
silently produces nothing is worse than an honest gap.

**Grafana dashboards.** `src/dashboards/odk-central-overview.json` with
panels for submissions per hour, API request rate and error rate (from
nginx logs via Loki if Prometheus has no HTTP metrics), pending-blob
count, Enketo cache hit rate, and pyxform conversion latency. Register
with `GrafanaDashboardProvider`.

**Alert rules.** `src/prometheus_alert_rules/odk-central.rule`:
- `/v1/version.json` failing for more than 2 minutes;
- pending-blob count rising for more than an hour with an `s3`
  relation present (the upload job has stalled);
- `redis-main` unreachable — this is the one piece of non-PostgreSQL
  state in the group;
- pyxform conversion failure rate above a threshold (a broken
  converter blocks all form publishing while everything else looks
  healthy).

**Deploy COS-Lite** in a second model, offer the endpoints
cross-model, and integrate all three charms.

**Commit:** `feat(charms): COS-Lite observability across the group`.

**Definition of done:** the dashboard renders with at least one
populated panel; Loki holds logs from all six workload services; alert
rules load without error in Prometheus.

**Goals:** A `jubilant` suite that exercises the whole group, including
the paths that only break across charm boundaries.

**`tests/integration/conftest.py`** — one module-scoped fixture
deploying the full composition from the Relation Surface section into a
`jubilant.temp_model()`, waiting for all applications active, then
running `create-admin` and yielding both the `Juju` handle and the
admin credentials.

**`tests/integration/test_deploy.py`:**
- `test_version_endpoint()` — `/v1/version.json` returns the Q3 version.
- `test_ui_reachable()` — the ingress URL returns 200 and HTML.
- `test_frontend_config_matches_domain()` — fetch
  `client-config.json` through the ingress and assert the origin
  matches `external-hostname`. This catches the baked-at-build-time
  frontend problem, which nothing else does.

**`tests/integration/test_form_lifecycle.py`** — the end-to-end test
that proves all three charms are actually cooperating:
1. Create a project via `POST /v1/projects`.
2. Upload `tests/data/minimal.xlsx` as a form
   (`POST /v1/projects/{id}/forms?ignoreWarnings=true`) — **this
   exercises `pyxform-k8s`**; a conversion failure surfaces here.

   shared API key**; a secrets mismatch surfaces here as a 403.
5. Submit an instance with an attachment via `POST .../submission`.
6. Read it back through the OData feed
   (`/v1/projects/{id}/forms/{xml}.svc/Submissions`) and assert the
   value round-trips.
7. With an `s3` relation, run `upload-pending-blobs` and assert the
   attachment is retrievable through the redirect.

**`tests/integration/test_secrets.py`:**
- `test_rotate_enketo_secrets()` — capture a working public form link,
  run `rotate-enketo-secrets`, wait for both applications active, and
  assert the form still renders. A rotation that reaches Central but
  not Enketo fails here with a 403, which is exactly the regression
  worth guarding.

**`tests/integration/test_upgrade.py`:**
- `test_refresh_charm()` — deploy, refresh all three charms to the
  freshly packed revision, assert Active regained and the form
  lifecycle test still passes.

**`tests/integration/test_day2.py`:**
- `test_backup_restore()` — backup, drop and recreate the database
  relation, restore, assert the project and form survive.
- `test_purge_deleted()` — soft-delete a form, purge with `force`,
  assert it is gone.

## Phase 12 — Release Scaffolding

**Goals:** First tagged release `0.1.0` with Charmhub upload wiring for
all three charms; uploadable but not published to a public channel.

**Steps:**

1. Populate `CHANGELOG.md` `[0.1.0]` with everything from Phases 1–11.

2. Tag and push:
   ```bash
   git tag -a 0.1.0 -m "chore(release): 0.1.0 — first production-ready release"
   git push origin 0.1.0
   ```

3. `.github/workflows/charmhub-upload.yml` — a matrix over the three
   charms, upload-only (track commented out):
   ```yaml
   name: Charmhub upload
   on:
     push:
       tags: ['*']
   jobs:
     upload:
       runs-on: ubuntu-latest
       strategy:
         matrix:
           charm: [odk-central-k8s, enketo-k8s, pyxform-k8s]
       steps:
         - uses: actions/checkout@v4
         - uses: canonical/charmcraft-actions/upload@v1
           with:
             credentials: ${{ secrets.CHARMHUB_TOKEN }}
             charm-path: charms/${{ matrix.charm }}
             charm-name: ${{ matrix.charm }}
             # track: <Q9-track>   # leave commented: upload-only
   ```

4. Register all three names at https://charmhub.io/register-charm
   (manual; cannot be automated) and add `CHARMHUB_TOKEN` to the
   repository secrets.

5. Verify the upload job produces a revision for each charm
   (`charmcraft status <name>`).

6. Write `RELEASE.md` describing the manual promotion path, and
   **state the group constraint explicitly**: the three charms are
   released together and `odk-central-k8s` and its `nginx-image` are
   version-locked to the same upstream tag. Promoting one charm alone
   is how this group breaks.

**Final commit:**
```bash
git commit -m "chore(release): 0.1.0 release scaffolding, Charmhub upload workflow

CHANGELOG 0.1.0 populated. Matrix charmhub-upload workflow across the
three charms (upload-only). RELEASE.md documents the promotion path and
the group version-lock constraint."
git push -u origin main
git push origin 0.1.0
```

**Definition of done:** three Charmhub revisions exist; none is in a
public channel.

options.description: Run `concierge prepare` with a Canonical Kubernetes (k8s snap) preset: installs juju, k8s, bootstraps a controller. Matches the prompt's stated preference. Takes ~10-20 min.

options.label: concierge, microk8s
options.description: Same tool, microk8s substrate. Better-trodden path for charm CI, but the prompt prefers k8s.

options.label: Manual install
options.description: I install the juju and k8s snaps directly and bootstrap by hand, no concierge. More control, more steps.

questions.question: Which public domain (Q6) should the deployment use? ODK Central will not work with a bare IP.

options.label: Auto nip.io (Recommended)
options.description: After traefik-k8s gets its LoadBalancer IP, I derive e.g. odk.10-0-0-5.nip.io and configure external-hostname with it. No DNS setup needed; works for the test deploy.

options.label: I'll supply an FQDN
options.description: Give me a real fully-qualified domain you control and have pointed at this box.

questions.question: Which email address for the initial Central admin (Q7)? Stored as a Juju secret, consumed by create-admin.

options.label: tony.meyer@gmail.com
options.description: Your account email. Used only as the local admin account identity in this test deployment.

options.label: ops-team@example.com
options.description: A placeholder address. Fine since no real SMTP relay is wired for the test deploy; mail delivery just won't work.

questions.question: Which GitHub namespace hosts the repo (Q1)? Note: `gh` is not installed, so I'd install it and you'd need to auth, or I can keep the work local.

options.label: tonyandrewmeyer
options.description: Create/push to tonyandrewmeyer/odk-central-operators. I'll install gh; you'll need to run `gh auth login` (or provide a token) when I hit the push.

options.label: Local only for now
options.description: Commit to the local git repo every phase as specified, but skip `git push` until you wire up a remote. Everything else proceeds unchanged.

questions.question: Day-one authentication mode (Q8)? This controls what the Phase 4 smoke test and Phase 10 integration suite authenticate with. OIDC is wired and tested in Phase 8 either way.

options.label: password (Recommended)
options.description: HTTP Basic + POST /v1/session work. create-admin yields a usable login, the form-lifecycle test can authenticate directly. The prompt's default.

options.label: oidc
options.description: Requires a working OIDC provider (hydra or external) before anything can authenticate at all. Disables password auth and POST /v1/session entirely upstream — the integration suite would need an OIDC token flow from day one.

options.label: in-charm (Recommended)
options.description: Two redis sidecar containers in enketo-k8s; redis-main gets Juju filesystem storage. Optional redis-main/redis-cache relations are still declared and take precedence when present. Phase 6 still probes redis-k8s latest/edge once and records the result.

options.label: relate
options.description: Depend on redis-k8s from latest/edge (revision 23, released 2022-12-05) as the primary path. Riskier — no stable Redis charm exists on Charmhub.

options.label: Defaults, latest track
options.description: odk-central-k8s, enketo-k8s, pyxform-k8s on the `latest` track; latest/edge → latest/candidate promotion path. Central's date-based versions make a version track impractical.

options.label: Something else
options.description: Supply alternative names or a track.

options.label: disabled (Recommended)
options.description: Charm blanks every SENTRY_* value unless an operator sets error-reporting-dsn. Nothing reports to ODK's telemetry.

options.label: I'll supply a DSN
options.description: Give me your own Sentry DSN to configure as the default.

ARG node_version=24.16.0



FROM node:${node_version}-slim AS pgdg
RUN apt-get update \
    && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
        ca-certificates \
        curl \
        gpg \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/* \
    && update-ca-certificates
RUN echo "deb http://apt.postgresql.org/pub/repos/apt/ $(grep -oP 'VERSION_CODENAME=\K\w+' /etc/os-release)-pgdg main" \
      | tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/pgdg.list \
    && curl https://www.postgresql.org/media/keys/ACCC4CF8.asc \
      | gpg --dearmor > /etc/apt/trusted.gpg.d/apt.postgresql.org.gpg



FROM node:${node_version}-slim AS intermediate
RUN apt-get update \
    && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
        git \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
COPY . .
RUN mkdir /tmp/sentry-versions
RUN git describe --tags --dirty --always > /tmp/sentry-versions/central
WORKDIR /server
RUN git describe --tags --dirty --always > /tmp/sentry-versions/server
WORKDIR /client
RUN git describe --tags --dirty --always > /tmp/sentry-versions/client



FROM node:${node_version}-slim

ARG node_version
LABEL org.opencontainers.image.source="https://github.com/getodk/central"

WORKDIR /usr/odk

COPY server/package*.json ./
COPY --from=pgdg /etc/apt/sources.list.d/pgdg.list \
    /etc/apt/sources.list.d/pgdg.list
COPY --from=pgdg /etc/apt/trusted.gpg.d/apt.postgresql.org.gpg \
    /etc/apt/trusted.gpg.d/apt.postgresql.org.gpg
RUN apt-get update \
    && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
        gpg \
        cron \
        procps \
        postgresql-client-14 \
        netcat-traditional \
        openssl \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/* \
    && npm clean-install --omit=dev --no-audit \
        --fund=false --update-notifier=false

COPY server/ ./
COPY files/shared/envsub.awk /scripts/
COPY files/service/scripts/ ./

COPY files/service/config.json.template /usr/share/odk/
COPY files/service/crontab /etc/cron.d/odk
COPY files/service/odk-cmd /usr/bin/
COPY files/service/with-pgenvblock.pl /usr/bin/

COPY --from=intermediate /tmp/sentry-versions/ ./sentry-versions

EXPOSE 8383

#!/bin/bash -eu
set -o pipefail
shopt -s inherit_errexit

log() { echo >&2 "[$(basename "$0")] $*"; }

assert_size() {
  local f="$1"
  local expectedSize="$2"

  if ! [[ -f "$f" ]]; then
    log "!!! File not found: $f"
    exit 1
  fi

  actualSize="$(stat -c "%s" "$f")"
  if ! [[ "$actualSize" = "$expectedSize" ]]; then
    log "!!!"
    log "!!! Unexpected file size:"
    log "!!!   file: $f"
    log "!!!   expected: $expectedSize b"
    log "!!!   actual:   $actualSize b"
    log "!!!"
    exit 1
  fi
}
if [[ "${ENKETO_SECRETS-}" = "danger-insecure" ]]; then
  log "Skipping secrets check."
else
  log "Checking secrets exist..."
  assert_size /etc/secrets/enketo-secret       64
  assert_size /etc/secrets/enketo-less-secret  32
  assert_size /etc/secrets/enketo-api-key     128
fi

CONFIG_PATH=${ENKETO_SRC_DIR}/config/config.json
log "Generating enketo configuration..."

BASE_URL=$( [ "${HTTPS_PORT}" = 443 ] && echo https://"${DOMAIN}" || echo https://"${DOMAIN}":"${HTTPS_PORT}" ) \
SECRET=$(cat /etc/secrets/enketo-secret) \
LESS_SECRET=$(cat /etc/secrets/enketo-less-secret) \
API_KEY=$(cat /etc/secrets/enketo-api-key) \
/scripts/envsub.awk \
    < "$CONFIG_PATH.template" \
    > "$CONFIG_PATH"

log "Starting enketo..."
exec yarn workspace enketo-express start

  echo "!!!"

  echo "!!!"

  echo "!!!"
  echo "!!! Please refer to the Central 2026.1.0 release notes for more information on this change."

===== setup-odk.sh (nginx) =====
#!/bin/bash -eu
set -o pipefail
shopt -s inherit_errexit

echo "writing client config..."
if [[ $OIDC_ENABLED != 'true' ]] && [[ $OIDC_ENABLED != 'false' ]]; then
  echo 'OIDC_ENABLED must be either true or false'
  exit 1
fi

/scripts/envsub.awk \
  < /usr/share/odk/nginx/client-config.json.template \
  > /usr/share/nginx/html/client-config.json

# Generate self-signed keys for the incorrect (catch-all) HTTPS listener.  This
# cert should never be seen by legitimate users, so it's not a big deal that
# it's self-signed and won't expire for 1,000 years.
mkdir -p /etc/nginx/ssl
openssl req -x509 -nodes -newkey rsa:2048 \
    -subj "/CN=invalid.local" \
    -keyout /etc/nginx/ssl/nginx.default.key \
    -out    /etc/nginx/ssl/nginx.default.crt \
    -days 365000

DH_PATH=/etc/dh/nginx.pem
if [ "$SSL_TYPE" != "upstream" ] && [ ! -s "$DH_PATH" ]; then
  openssl dhparam -out "$DH_PATH" 2048
fi

SELFSIGN_PATH="/etc/selfsign/live/$DOMAIN"
if [ "$SSL_TYPE" = "selfsign" ] && [ ! -s "$SELFSIGN_PATH/privkey.pem" ]; then
  mkdir -p "$SELFSIGN_PATH"
  openssl req -x509 -newkey rsa:4096 \
    -subj "/C=XX/ST=XXXX/L=XXXX/O=XXXX/CN=localhost" \
    -keyout "$SELFSIGN_PATH/privkey.pem" \
    -out "$SELFSIGN_PATH/fullchain.pem" \
    -days 3650 -nodes -sha256
fi

# start from fresh templates in case ssl type has changed
echo "writing fresh nginx templates..."
# redirector.conf gets deleted if using upstream SSL so copy it back
/scripts/envsub.awk \
  < /usr/share/odk/nginx/redirector.conf \
  > /etc/nginx/conf.d/redirector.conf

CERT_DOMAIN=$( [ "$SSL_TYPE" = "customssl" ] && echo "local" || echo "$DOMAIN") \
SENTRY_DSN_FRONTEND_ROOT="$(awk 'sub(/:\/\/[a-z0-9]*@/, "://") && sub(/\/[0-9]+$/, "")' <<<"$SENTRY_DSN_FRONTEND")" \
/scripts/envsub.awk \
  < /usr/share/odk/nginx/odk.conf.template \
  > /etc/nginx/conf.d/odk.conf

if [ "$SSL_TYPE" = "letsencrypt" ]; then
  echo "starting nginx for letsencrypt..."
  /bin/bash /scripts/start_nginx_certbot.sh
else
  if [ "$SSL_TYPE" = "upstream" ]; then
    # no need for letsencrypt challenge reply or 80 to 443 redirection
    rm -f /etc/nginx/conf.d/redirector.conf
    # strip out all ssl_* directives
    perl -i -ne 's/listen 443.*/listen 80;/; print if ! /\bssl_/' /etc/nginx/conf.d/odk.conf
    # force https because we expect SSL upstream
    perl -i -pe 's/X-Forwarded-Proto \$scheme/X-Forwarded-Proto https/;' /etc/nginx/conf.d/odk.conf
    echo "starting nginx for upstream ssl..."
  else
    # remove letsencrypt challenge reply, but keep 80 to 443 redirection
    perl -i -ne 'print if $. < 9 || $. > 16' /etc/nginx/conf.d/redirector.conf
    echo "starting nginx for custom ssl and self-signed certs..."
  fi
  exec nginx -g "daemon off;"
fi

===== docker-compose.yml =====
services:
  postgres14:
    build:
      context: .
      dockerfile: postgres14.dockerfile
    shm_size: 512m
    volumes:
      - postgres14:/var/lib/odk/postgresql/14
    environment:
      POSTGRES_USER: odk
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: odk
      POSTGRES_DB: odk
    restart: always
  postgres:
    # This service upgrades from postgres 9.6 to 14.
    # The legacy name must be maintained to allow access to the anonymous volume.
    build:
      context: .
      dockerfile: postgres-upgrade.dockerfile
    platform: linux/amd64
    volumes:
      - /var/lib/postgresql/data
      - postgres14:/var/lib/postgresql/14
      - ./files/postgres14/upgrade:/postgres14-upgrade
    environment:
      PGUSER: odk
      POSTGRES_INITDB_ARGS: -U odk
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: odk
      POSTGRES_DB: odk
  mail:
    image: "registry.gitlab.com/egos-tech/smtp:1.2.8"
    volumes:
      - ./files/mail/rsa.private:/etc/exim4/dkim.key.temp:ro
    environment:
      - MAILNAME=${DOMAIN}
      - DKIM_KEY_PATH=/etc/exim4/dkim.key.temp
    restart: always
  service:
    build:
      context: .
      dockerfile: service.dockerfile
    depends_on:
      - secrets
      - postgres14
      - mail
      - pyxform
      - enketo
    volumes:
      - secrets:/etc/secrets
    env_file:
      - ".env"
    environment:
      - DOMAIN=${DOMAIN}
      - SYSADMIN_EMAIL=${SYSADMIN_EMAIL}
      - HTTPS_PORT=${HTTPS_PORT:-443}
      - NODE_OPTIONS=${SERVICE_NODE_OPTIONS:-}
      # Prepare libpq connection env vars, while handling legacy DB_* vars.
      # Resolution order:
      # 1. PGVAR specified in .env. This includes declarations with empty values, for instance, to use an empty password (PGPASSWORD=).
      # 2. Corresponding legacy DB_VAR in .env. These are legacy overrides for custom database connections.
      # 3. ODK default value.
      - PGHOST=${PGHOST-${DB_HOST:-postgres14}}
      - PGDATABASE=${PGDATABASE-${DB_NAME:-odk}}
      - PGUSER=${PGUSER-${DB_USER:-odk}}
      - PGPASSWORD=${PGPASSWORD-${DB_PASSWORD:-odk}}
      - PGAPPNAME=${PGAPPNAME-odkcentral}
      # End of libpq connection env var preparation.
      - DB_SSL=${DB_SSL:-null}
      - DB_POOL_SIZE=${DB_POOL_SIZE:-10}
      - EMAIL_FROM=${EMAIL_FROM:-no-reply@$DOMAIN}
      - EMAIL_HOST=${EMAIL_HOST:-mail}
      - EMAIL_PORT=${EMAIL_PORT:-25}
      - EMAIL_SECURE=${EMAIL_SECURE:-false}
      - EMAIL_IGNORE_TLS=${EMAIL_IGNORE_TLS:-true}
      - EMAIL_USER=${EMAIL_USER:-}
      - EMAIL_PASSWORD=${EMAIL_PASSWORD:-}
      - OIDC_ENABLED=${OIDC_ENABLED:-false}
      - OIDC_ISSUER_URL=${OIDC_ISSUER_URL:-}
      - OIDC_CLIENT_ID=${OIDC_CLIENT_ID:-}
      - OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET=${OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET:-}
      - SENTRY_ORG_SUBDOMAIN=${SENTRY_ORG_SUBDOMAIN:-o130137}
      - SENTRY_KEY=${SENTRY_KEY:-3cf75f54983e473da6bd07daddf0d2ee}
      - SENTRY_PROJECT=${SENTRY_PROJECT:-1298632}
      - SENTRY_TRACE_RATE=${SENTRY_TRACE_RATE:-0.1}
      - S3_SERVER=${S3_SERVER:-}
      - S3_ACCESS_KEY=${S3_ACCESS_KEY:-}
      - S3_SECRET_KEY=${S3_SECRET_KEY:-}
      - S3_BUCKET_NAME=${S3_BUCKET_NAME:-}
      - SESSION_LIFETIME=${SESSION_LIFETIME:-86400}
    command: [ "./start-odk.sh" ]
    restart: always

content.text:
`concierge` is installing Canonical Kubernetes (`k8s 1.32-classic/stable`) — good, that's the preferred substrate.

Two landmines found in the nginx template that change the design:

1. `odk.conf.template` **hardcodes** `proxy_pass http://enketo:8005` and `http://service:8383`. `service` is same-pod (fine as localhost), but `enketo` is a separate Juju application — that hostname will never resolve. The charm must push its own templates into `/usr/share/odk/nginx/` (which is exactly what upstream's compose bind-mount does).
2. `/csp-report` proxies to `https://${SENTRY_ORG_SUBDOMAIN}.ingest.sentry.io/api/${SENTRY_PROJECT}/...`. Naively blanking `SENTRY_*` per Q10 yields `https://.ingest.sentry.io/api//security/` — nginx fails to load that config. Blanking has to *remove* the block, not just empty the variables.

Starting the Phase 1 scaffold while k8s installs.

cat > README.md <<'EOF'
# odk-central-operators

Juju charms for [ODK Central](https://getodk.org/), an open-source platform for
collecting, managing and using survey and field data.

[![CI](https://github.com/tonyandrewmeyer/odk-central-operators/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/tonyandrewmeyer/odk-central-operators/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
[![License: Apache 2.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-Apache_2.0-blue.svg)](LICENSE)

## What is ODK Central?

ODK Central is the server half of the [ODK](https://getodk.org/) ecosystem:
forms authored as XLSForm spreadsheets are converted to XForms, filled in
offline on a mobile client or in a browser, and submitted back to Central. It
manages projects, form versions, submissions, attachments and users, and
exposes everything over a REST and OData API.

## The charm group

Upstream ships ODK Central as an eight-container Docker Compose stack. This
repository deploys it as **three Juju applications** that are designed to be
deployed together.

| Charm | Containers | What it runs |
|---|---|---|
| `odk-central-k8s` | `service`, `nginx` | The Central API (Node/pm2) and the nginx reverse proxy serving the built frontend. Released and version-locked together upstream. |
| `enketo-k8s` | `enketo`, `redis-main`, `redis-cache` | [Enketo](https://github.com/enketo/enketo), which renders XForms as web forms, plus its two Redis instances (durable and cache). |
| `pyxform-k8s` | `pyxform` | The stateless [pyxform](https://github.com/XLSForm/pyxform) HTTP service that converts XLSForm spreadsheets to XForms. |

Upstream's one-shot `secrets` container has no charm equivalent: Juju has no
shared volume between applications, so `odk-central-k8s` generates the three
shared Enketo secrets itself, stores them as application-owned Juju secrets and
distributes them over the `odk-enketo` relation. See
[`docs/architecture.md`](docs/architecture.md).

## Quick start

```bash
juju add-model odk

juju deploy odk-central-k8s --channel latest/edge --trust
juju deploy enketo-k8s      --channel latest/edge
juju deploy pyxform-k8s     --channel latest/edge

juju deploy postgresql-k8s --channel 16/stable --trust
juju deploy traefik-k8s    --channel latest/stable --trust

juju integrate odk-central-k8s postgresql-k8s
juju integrate odk-central-k8s pyxform-k8s
juju integrate odk-central-k8s enketo-k8s
juju integrate odk-central-k8s traefik-k8s

juju config odk-central-k8s external-hostname=odk.example.com

SECRET_ID=$(juju add-secret odk-admin-email email=ops-team@example.com)
juju grant-secret "$SECRET_ID" odk-central-k8s
juju config odk-central-k8s admin-email-secret="$SECRET_ID"
juju run odk-central-k8s/0 create-admin
```

The full walkthrough, from an empty model to a first submission, is in
[`docs/quickstart.md`](docs/quickstart.md).

## Relation matrix

| Charm | Endpoint | Interface | Role | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `odk-central-k8s` | `odk-enketo` | `odk-enketo` | provides | Ships the three shared secrets and the public base URL to Enketo; receives Enketo's in-cluster URL back |
| `odk-central-k8s` | `postgresql` | `postgresql_client` | requires | Central's application database |
| `odk-central-k8s` | `xlsform` | `odk-xlsform` | requires | pyxform host and port |
| `odk-central-k8s` | `ingress` | `ingress` | requires | Public HTTP ingress via traefik |
| `odk-central-k8s` | `s3` | `s3` | requires | Blob store for submission attachments and form media |
| `odk-central-k8s` | `smtp` | `smtp` | requires | Account creation and password reset email |
| `odk-central-k8s` | `oauth` | `oauth` | requires | OpenID Connect via the Canonical Identity Platform |
| `odk-central-k8s` | `logging` / `metrics-endpoint` / `grafana-dashboard` / `tracing` | COS | requires | Observability |
| `enketo-k8s` | `odk-enketo` | `odk-enketo` | requires | Shared secrets and base URL from Central |
| `enketo-k8s` | `redis-main` / `redis-cache` | `redis` | requires (optional) | External Redis instead of the in-charm sidecars |
| `enketo-k8s` | `logging` / `metrics-endpoint` / `grafana-dashboard` | COS | requires | Observability |
| `pyxform-k8s` | `xlsform` | `odk-xlsform` | provides | Advertises its host and port to Central |
| `pyxform-k8s` | `logging` / `metrics-endpoint` | COS | requires | Observability |

`pyxform-k8s` has no ingress endpoint on purpose: it is reached only by
Central, in-cluster, and must not be exposed.

## Day-2 operations

| Charm | Action | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `odk-central-k8s` | `create-admin` | Create the initial web user from the `odk-admin-email` Juju secret and promote it to administrator. Returns the password once. |
| `odk-central-k8s` | `promote-user` | Grant an existing user the administrator role. |
| `odk-central-k8s` | `reset-password` | Reset a user's password and return the new value once. |
| `odk-central-k8s` | `rotate-enketo-secrets` | Regenerate all three shared Enketo secrets, republish them over the relation and restart both workloads. |
| `odk-central-k8s` | `run-migrations` | Run database migrations manually. |
| `odk-central-k8s` | `upload-pending-blobs` | Move submission attachments still held in PostgreSQL to the S3 blob store. |
| `odk-central-k8s` | `purge-deleted` | Permanently remove soft-deleted forms and submissions. |
| `odk-central-k8s` | `backup` | `pg_dump` the Central database to the S3 blob store. |
| `odk-central-k8s` | `restore` | Restore the Central database from a backup snapshot. |
| `enketo-k8s` | `flush-cache` | Flush the cache Redis instance only, never the durable one. |
| `enketo-k8s` | `redis-info` | Return `INFO` output from both Redis instances. |
| `pyxform-k8s` | `convert` | Convert a base64-encoded XLSForm and return the XForm. Diagnostic only. |

Full detail, including what each one does to running users, is in
[`docs/day2-ops.md`](docs/day2-ops.md).

## Observability

All three charms are COS-Lite ready. `odk-central-k8s` and `enketo-k8s` forward
every Pebble service's logs to Loki, expose Prometheus metrics, and ship a
Grafana dashboard and alert rules covering API availability, pending blob
uploads, Redis reachability and pyxform conversion failures.

```bash
juju integrate odk-central-k8s grafana-k8s
juju integrate odk-central-k8s prometheus-k8s
juju integrate odk-central-k8s loki-k8s
```

See [`docs/observability.md`](docs/observability.md).

## Contributing

See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md).

## Licence

Apache 2.0. So is every piece of the workload these charms deploy — see
[CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md#licensing).

# Contributing

Thanks for your interest in improving the ODK Central charms.

## Repository layout

```
charms/odk-central-k8s/   # Central API + nginx/frontend
charms/enketo-k8s/        # Enketo web forms + its two Redis instances
charms/pyxform-k8s/       # XLSForm -> XForm conversion service
hack/upstream/            # Verbatim upstream reference files, pinned to the targeted release
docs/                     # mkdocs-material site covering all three charms
tests/integration/        # Group-level jubilant tests; there are no per-charm integration tests
scripts/                  # Repository tooling (docs checks, and so on)
```

The three charms live in one repository because they are deployed, released and
version-locked as a group. See [RELEASE.md](RELEASE.md).

## Development setup

Dependencies are managed with [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/), which drives a
workspace spanning the three charm directories.

```bash
curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh
uv sync
uv run pre-commit install --install-hooks
uv run pre-commit install --hook-type commit-msg
```

## Tests

Unit tests use [`ops.testing`](https://ops.readthedocs.io/en/latest/reference/ops-testing.html).
Do not add `pytest-operator`; this repository does not use it.

```bash
uv run pytest charms/odk-central-k8s/tests/unit
uv run pytest charms/enketo-k8s/tests/unit
uv run pytest charms/pyxform-k8s/tests/unit
```

Integration tests use [`jubilant`](https://github.com/canonical/jubilant) and
exercise the whole group at once, because the interesting failures in this
charm group only happen across charm boundaries.

```bash
uv run pytest tests/integration -v
```

They need a bootstrapped Kubernetes controller and take roughly half an hour.

### Kubernetes flavour

The dev-box workflow targets [Canonical
Kubernetes](https://documentation.ubuntu.com/canonical-kubernetes/) (the `k8s`
snap), which is what the charms are developed against. CI runs the integration
job on **microk8s** instead, because Canonical Kubernetes is not yet available
as a packaged GitHub Actions provider. If you hit a failure that reproduces on
one and not the other, say which flavour in the issue — that difference is
worth knowing about.

## Building

```bash
cd charms/odk-central-k8s && charmcraft pack
```

`charmcraft` 4.x and `ops` 3.x are required; do not pin below those majors.

## Upstream reference files

`hack/upstream/` holds verbatim copies of the upstream `getodk/central` files
that determine how the workload starts: the compose file, the config templates,
the nginx setup script and the Redis configs. They are pinned to the release the
charms currently target.

**Upstream's files are authoritative.** When they disagree with anything in this
repository's docs or code, upstream wins and the charm is the thing that needs
fixing. When bumping the targeted release, refresh `hack/upstream/` first and
read the diff before touching charm code.

## Style

- `ruff` for linting and formatting, line length 99, target `py312`.
- `mypy --strict` on charm source. Vendored charm libraries under
  `charms/*/lib/` are excluded; they are not ours to type.
- `yamllint` and `actionlint` on YAML and workflows.

`uv run pre-commit run --all-files` runs the lot, and CI runs exactly that.

## Commits and pull requests

This repository uses [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/)
and [release-please](https://github.com/googleapis/release-please). The commit
subject determines the changelog entry and the version bump, so it matters.

```
feat(enketo): stop the redis sidecar when a redis relation is present
fix(central): blank the upstream Sentry DSN in the nginx environment
docs: explain why rotating Enketo secrets logs everyone out
```

Scopes in use: `central`, `enketo`, `pyxform`, `charms` (cross-cutting), `docs`,
`ci`.

Development happens directly on `main`. Pull requests are welcome from outside
contributors; please make sure `uv run pre-commit run --all-files` passes and
that unit tests cover the change.

## Licensing

Everything here is Apache-2.0, and — unusually for this software category — so
is everything it deploys. `getodk/central`, `central-backend`,
`central-frontend`, `pyxform` and `enketo/enketo` are all Apache-2.0, and the
published container images contain no enterprise-gated or
source-available-but-not-open code. There is no licence divergence between the
charms and the workload to document, and no feature behind a commercial licence
that these charms cannot reach.

That is a large part of why this upstream was chosen.
EOF

cat > SECURITY.md <<'EOF'
# Security policy

## Reporting a vulnerability in these charms

Please report security issues in the charms to **security@ubuntu.com**.

Include as much of the following as you can:

- which charm is affected (`odk-central-k8s`, `enketo-k8s`, `pyxform-k8s`);
- the charm revision and channel, and the ODK Central release it deploys;
- Juju version and Kubernetes flavour;
- what an attacker can achieve, and the steps to reproduce it.

You will get an acknowledgement within **5 business days**. We follow
coordinated disclosure: please give us a reasonable window to ship a fix before
publishing details.

Canonical's full disclosure policy is at
<https://ubuntu.com/security/disclosure-policy>.

## Reporting a vulnerability in ODK Central itself

If the issue is in the upstream workload rather than in the charm code — the
Central API, the frontend, Enketo or pyxform — report it to the ODK project at
<https://github.com/getodk/central/security>. Please let us know as well, so we
can track the fix and pin a patched release.

## Scope notes

- Every credential these charms handle is a Juju secret. If you find a way to
  read one out of `juju config`, charm logs, action output beyond the single
  intended return, or a rendered config file readable by an unexpected
  container, that is in scope.
- The three shared Enketo secrets are generated by `odk-central-k8s` and granted
  to `enketo-k8s` over a relation. Anything that lets a third application obtain
  them is in scope.
- These charms deliberately terminate TLS at `traefik-k8s` and run the workload
  nginx on plain HTTP behind it. Reports that "the workload serves HTTP" are not
  vulnerabilities on their own; a way to reach the workload port bypassing
  ingress is.
EOF

Because the three charms in this repository are released as a group, one
changelog covers all of them. Entries are prefixed with the charm they affect.

on:
  push:

      - run: uv sync --frozen
      - run: uv run pre-commit run --all-files --show-diff-on-failure

  unit-tests:
    name: Unit tests (${{ matrix.charm }})
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        charm: [odk-central-k8s, enketo-k8s, pyxform-k8s]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v5

      - name: Run unit tests

        with:

      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v5
